standard: Near-photoreal AAA forest art against the supplied warm, lush forest reference. Score is based on the rendered screenshots, independent of implementation effort and performance.
summary: A recognizable and playable-looking forest prototype, with readable bark, ground detail and a coherent trail. It remains far below near-photoreal AAA: repeated rigid grass, pole-like trees, exposed empty horizon and uniform material treatment are immediately visible. Golden haze helps the trail mood but does not overcome the artificial vegetation and staging.

issues.evidence: Both views have thin upright grass stalks with dark, blunt-looking bases, arranged in continuous narrow bands along the path. Large areas of leaf-textured soil remain visible between stalks. Foreground bushes show repeated flat green leaves; the reference has broad, curved, overlapping grass masses.
issues.action: Make the dominant grass blades visibly curved and tapered with varied lean and height. Group several blade shapes into dense irregular clumps, overlap their bases with low moss/leaf litter, and break the path-edge bands with gaps, fern colonies and grass extending irregularly into the trail. Judge improvement from the same ground-level cameras, not instance count.

issues.evidence: Grove exposes a nearly empty pale ground strip beneath a large blue sky opening at the path terminus; isolated saplings make the scene boundary easy to read. The massive foreground trunk and rock consume much of the right side without revealing a compelling destination. Trail also shows bright empty gaps between trunks.
issues.action: Build a layered destination around a bend: a low terrain rise, staggered middle-distance trees, dense shrub masses and a darker distant tree wall. Conceal the bare horizon from both named views. Shift the grove camera clear of the huge trunk enough to reveal this composition while retaining a smaller foreground framing element.

issues.evidence: Rows of long, mostly straight branchless trunks rise into similar dense, lumpy crowns. Their repeated vertical rhythm dominates both images; the smaller trees repeat the same tiered silhouette. The foreground trees have little root flare or convincing transition into the forest floor.
issues.action: Create at least three clearly different tree families with different trunk taper, lean, crown start height and branch asymmetry. Give near trees visible root flares and a few substantial irregular limbs, vary crown gaps, and compose local age groups with fallen wood or broken trunks to interrupt the repeated poles.

issues.evidence: Trail's right and middle distance are covered by a pale yellow veil that suppresses leaf and trunk separation. Grove instead reveals a saturated blue opening with a relatively flat beige horizon. The reference has a stronger relationship between shaded green understory, warm illuminated grass edges and localized shafts of light.
issues.action: Reduce the uniform near-camera haze and preserve darker, greener shaded foliage. Concentrate warm scattering along the sun direction and into depth, with a few broad interrupted light shafts or equivalent localized lighting. Tune sky, fog and exposure together so the same golden forest mood survives both camera directions without washing out the midground.

issues.evidence: The prominent trail and grove rocks share an evenly distributed green cracked texture over rounded forms. The path is uniformly dry tan, with small angular debris scattered across it; roots, compressed path edges and localized moisture are absent. Fine texture exists, but the larger forms and material transitions remain generic.
issues.action: Give the foreground rocks distinct fractured silhouettes and material zones: exposed stone faces, moss concentrated on sheltered upper surfaces and darker contact at soil. Add a few exposed roots crossing into the path, clustered gravel and litter near edges, and broad damp/compacted dirt variation to connect objects to the ground.

metricsContext.capture: Headless Chromium 151 on Apple M1 Pro/ANGLE Metal; 1600x1000, pixel ratio 1, high quality, default sliders.
metricsContext.errors: No console, page, request or WebGL errors recorded in either capture.
metricsContext.caveat: Browser scheduling measurements are context, not a production FPS guarantee; they do not affect the art score.
